answer: An ivory beacon marks a karst rescue depot. Its buyer ranks vendors by verified value delivered on its own orders. The buyer signs receipts binding order, value and vendor, and counts each order once. A hundred aliases endorsing one another gain no rank. Moving up takes real deliveries or compromising the buyer's records. Newcomers compete for one small trial budget, so aliases cannot multiply trial exposure. Entry is slower, and a vendor can still defect after building trust.
